r1-handoff.finding: g2 shipped mechanical_fields, emit_mechanical_snapshot on the g1 seam, the refusals counter, CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md and the EPISODE_STORE.md rewrite - all four handoff deliverables present. Correctness defects are recorded against the hunt items, not here.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift / engine-diff-is-zero-logic ruling
r2-scope.imperative: Confirm the engine diff is the ruled shape (import shim, two call lines, base_dir threading, plus the in-scope refusals counter) and nothing more. Record pass/fail.
r2-scope.finding: Engine diff is 65 added lines across two hunks: claim() gains one setdefault line plus comment, main() refusal path gains a 3-line guarded increment plus comment. No verb logic altered, no control flow changed. Matches the zero-logic ruling plus the in-scope refusals counter. Verified by reading git diff 967493c..HEAD on scripts/checklist_engine.py.

h1-proof-audit.title: HUNT 1.1 audit the Commander's reopens over-count proof
h1-proof-audit.imperative: Audit the repro at .agent-work/issue-305/evidence/hunt1_reopens_overcount.py: is it sound, or narrower than claimed? Determine whether a reachable continuation exists after a rework-cap escalation (is skip realistic; does resume refuse per :1811-1817). Rule LIVE or LATENT.
h1-proof-audit.finding: PROOF SOUND, DEFECT LIVE. Audited at source and re-derived independently. skip is not merely a realistic continuation, it is the ONLY one: skip has no status guard at all (line 1765), resume refuses a cap-escalation for want of prior_status (1811-1817, confirmed), reopen refuses a blocked gate, and start refuses because active_id returns the blocked gate itself since TERMINAL is complete-or-skipped only. resume's own refusal text names skip as the sanctioned exit. So the Commander's route is canonical, not contrived. Additional measurement the proof did not make: the over-count magnitude is E at a start seam but E-1 at a reopen seam, because the in-flight reopen's own journal line is not yet written. My independent two-gate repro with one escalation therefore came back green - the lag cancelled the single escalation exactly. That NARROWS the proof to the start seam without weakening it.

h1-class-sweep.title: HUNT 1.2 same-class sweep over failed-commands, rework-count, refusals
h1-class-sweep.imperative: For each of failed-commands, rework-count, refusals: enumerate EVERY branch that writes the witness and confirm none can move it in the unexpected direction. Record findings per field.
h1-class-sweep.finding: Swept all three. rework-count CLEAN: the only writer is reopen's success branch at 1880 (+1); the escalation branch at 1870-1879 deliberately does not touch it, which is precisely why this field is right and reopens is wrong; amend-add initialises 0; amend-drop and amend-rescope refuse any non-pending gate, so the only loss is a whole task disappearing, which surfaces as a refusal not a wrong value. failed-commands CLEAN: the only writer is _check_condition's command branch at 771; the git-change-policy branch writes type artifact-policy, not command-output; nothing anywhere deletes evidence, and reopen supersedes rather than removes. Re-running a failing check appends another item, which test_failed_commands_tracks_real_non_zero_command_checks pins deliberately as 2, so retry inflation is stated intent. refusals NOT CLEAN: a foreign session's lease-conflict refusal increments the owning run's tally. Measured - claim as own, then start with session-id SOMEONE-ELSE, exit 1, counter went 1 to 2. The field is FILE-scoped, not run-scoped as both the schema doc and the composer comment assert. Same class as HUNT 1: a witness assumed attributable to this run is movable in the over-counting direction by a party outside it, and in a constellation any teammate touching a crew's checklist does it.

h1-fix-shape.title: HUNT 1.3 rule on fix shape A/B/C
h1-fix-shape.imperative: Verify the load-bearing premise of option A (escalations are countable via cl['blockers'] and resume cannot clear them). Check whether the docstring's no-journal-yet reason survives as a reason to keep the journal witness at all. Rule A/B/C with reasoning. Do NOT implement.
h1-fix-shape.finding: Option A's load-bearing premise CONFIRMED at source: the escalation appends a distinctive blockers entry (blocker text rework cap N exceeded, next_action escalate do not re-dispatch) and nothing can remove it - resume refuses the gate before reaching its blockers filter, amend-drop refuses a non-pending gate, and skip leaves blockers untouched. So escalations are durably countable and A is arithmetically sound at both seams. I nonetheless rule for B. Reasons: A keeps the over-counting witness and compensates by string-matching engine-authored human-readable text from episode_capture, a new cross-module coupling in the module ruled to not change engine behaviour, so a reworded message silently regresses to over-counting; A fixes the instance, B removes the class. The docstring's stated reason for the journal does NOT survive - it argues against a journal-ONLY source, and _rework_total is not journal-only: it reads in memory and returns 0, never None, for a well-formed checklist, so B has no first-mutating-verb gap at all. B also deletes find_spine_path and journal_reopens, about 60 lines whose sole purpose is feeding a max that my mutation M5 proves nothing tests. B's real cost is losing amend-drop recovery, an under-count on a narrow path that is itself untested today. C rejected: the witnesses legitimately disagree in the amend case, so refusing would blank the field in ordinary runs. WHICHEVER is chosen must ship with a test that mutation M5 fails - that is the actual deliverable, not the arithmetic.

h2-derivation.title: HUNT 2 per-field derivation trace (not constants)
h2-derivation.imperative: For each of the eleven fields, trace it to the engine state it derives from and construct a run with a NON-DEFAULT true value; confirm the composer tracks it. Include: project REFUSES with no git. Do not accept validate_delta() as evidence of anything but shape.
h2-derivation.finding: All eleven traced to engine state, and the constant-returning defect is excluded by mutation rather than by inspection. run from checklist work_id; project from git rev-parse --git-common-dir parent, verified to REFUSE outside a repo (my hunt1 temp-dir run emitted no project key) and verified NOT to use durable_root, which would name the epic worktree; role from engine_session.claimed_by; spine-step from the imported active_id, not re-derived; rework-count from the task counter; failed-commands from engine-written command-output evidence; reopens from two witnesses (defective, see h1); context-manifest-ref from the manifest's own blob OID, which the implementer matched against git hash-object in the world; artifact-ref from the engine's own _collect_changed_files; refusals from the armed counter. Non-default values confirmed live: reopens 1 and 2, failed-commands 1 and 2, rework-count 1, refusals 1 and 2. validate_delta was not relied on for anything but shape.

h2-refusals.title: HUNT 2a refusals counter: additive, refusal-path-only
h2-refusals.imperative: Construct a checklist saved BEFORE the counter existed; confirm every reader still works. Induce a SUCCESSFUL verb and assert the counter did NOT move. Confirm increment is on the refusal path only.
h2-refusals.finding: Additivity PROVEN in the world, not argued. Built a pre-counter checklist (claimed, then the refusals key deleted): engine current still exits 0, a successful start still works, a real refusal leaves the key ABSENT rather than writing 1, mechanical_fields refuses the field, and a manifest still builds. Did-NOT-move PROVEN: after a successful start the counter stayed 0; after the next refused start it read exactly 1; a --dry-run refusal left it at 1. Arming confirmed to sit after claim's idempotent-resume early return at line 931, so a same-session re-claim cannot backdate a 0. The counter itself is monotone and correctly guarded against bool. Its scoping is the defect and is recorded under h1-class-sweep.

h2-docs.title: HUNT 2a/2c docs truth: CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md and EPISODE_STORE.md:781
h2-docs.imperative: Confirm docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md documents refusals and matches the implementation exactly. Confirm the EPISODE_STORE.md:781 rewrite is TRUE as written and no longer promises automated episode creation that _validate_create forbids. Verify the #344 latency claim.
h2-docs.finding: EPISODE_STORE.md:781 is TRUE AS WRITTEN - confirmed against apply_episode_delta._validate_create at 865-925: agent_supplied is required, must contain EXACTLY the five AGENT_SUPPLIED_KINDS with no extras, and each payload is validated non-empty, so a complete episode genuinely cannot exist without agent judgement and the rewrite no longer promises automated creation. The #344 latency claim is TRUE and correctly stated: both halves live in scripts/ and reach runs only via installed bundles, and this run's own snapshot carries refused refusals, which is that latency visible rather than papered over. CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md does NOT match the implementation on two points. First, it states the field is written by the CLI boundary alone, never by a verb function, but the arming write cl.setdefault refusals 0 is inside claim(), a verb function - the doc's own next bullet says armed by claim, so it contradicts itself. Second, it justifies run-scoping because a refusal does not always name a task, citing an unknown item id, a lease conflict, and A MALFORMED VERB - but a malformed verb exits through argparse with code 2 before the checklist is ever loaded, so it is never counted. Measured: engine frobnicate a exits 2 and leaves the counter unmoved. Both are inaccuracies in a doc the ruling required to ship in the same PR.

h2-predicate.title: HUNT 2d predicate-is-whole-condition audit
h2-predicate.imperative: Audit the counter's and the tallies' tests: boundary predicates need cases BOTH sides; collection quantifiers need a MULTI-ELEMENT case; a test env that cannot reach the failing condition is vacuous.
h2-predicate.finding: Mostly met, one real gap. failed-commands has both sides (a failing check counted, a passing check explicitly not) and a multi-element case (asserted 2). refusals has both sides (a refusal moves it, a successful verb does not) plus the pre-counter absence case. project has repo, linked-worktree-under-epic-lease, and non-repository. GAP: find_spine_path's predicate is matches[0] if len(matches)==1 else None - a collection quantifier with a 2-or-more branch that no test reaches. There is no multi-element case and no zero-match case. That branch is the guard against reading another run's journal as this one's, and multi-checklist work areas are live in this very repo (.agent-work/issue-305/ holds both spine.json and execute.json with journals). Lesser: reopen_total's own test admits in its docstring that mechanical_fields would never reach the branch it tests, so it is exercised only on the helper directly; and the refusals>=0 predicate has no non-int or negative case.

h2-mutation.title: HUNT 2b independent mutation the implementer did not ship
h2-mutation.imperative: Devise and apply a mutation the implementer's red-proof does not cover. Break the CALL SITE, not the callee, to test whether wiring is real. Run the suite; confirm it catches. Revert.
h2-mutation.finding: Seven independent call-site mutations, none of them the implementer's. Six CAUGHT: M1 deleting the emit_mechanical_snapshot call inside emit_step_manifest (the wiring-is-ceremonial test) - caught; M2 deleting the increment in main's refusal path - caught; M3 deleting the setdefault arming in claim - caught; M4 replacing failed_command_count with the constant 0 - caught; M6 replacing rework-count with the constant 0 - caught; M7 making project fall back to a guess instead of refusing - caught. So the wiring is real and the constant-returning defect this gate exists to catch is genuinely excluded. M5 SURVIVED and is a blocker: replacing the whole two-witness reopen_total call with _rework_total alone leaves all 63 episode tests green. The max reconciliation - the most intricate part of the composer, the exact locus of the HUNT 1 defect, and the thing find_spine_path and journal_reopens exist solely to feed - has NO discriminating test. The implementer cited test_reopens_is_run_scoped_where_rework_count_is_step_scoped as pinning a run where the two differ, but that test distinguishes RUN scope from STEP scope, and the run-scoped _rework_total sums to the same 2, so it does not discriminate the journal witness at all. Every mutation was reverted; git diff --stat on scripts/ is empty.

h3-asymmetry.title: HUNT 3 confirm/overturn the three source claims + snapshot collision
h3-asymmetry.imperative: Independently confirm or overturn: (i) write_manifest returns Path(path) so the collapsed return is value-identical; (ii) emit_mechanical_snapshot swallows every exception; (iii) the write-if-absent vs overwrite asymmetry is documented+justified. Then rule on the start/reopen snapshot_path collision: right by design or by accident.
h3-asymmetry.finding: All three source claims CONFIRMED independently. (i) context_manifest.write_manifest ends with return destination where destination is Path(path), so the collapsed return destination in emit_step_manifest is value-identical to the old return cm.write_manifest(...) - and the collapse also preserves write-if-absent, since the guard tests the same destination the write uses. (ii) emit_mechanical_snapshot's except Exception at 562-563 returns None, so no snapshot failure can reach emit_step_manifest's stub path; one precision correction to the claim as worded - it swallows every Exception, not every BaseException, so a KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit still propagates, which is correct and matches emit_step_manifest's own except. (iii) the asymmetry is documented and justified at 514-521 and the justification holds: the pin is over the MANIFEST's bytes, so refreshing the snapshot costs the manifest guarantee nothing. RULING on the start/reopen collision: right by DESIGN, not by accident, and I confirmed nothing depends on the original - grep finds no reader of the mechanical/ path anywhere in scripts/ outside the writer itself, and context-manifest-ref pins the manifest, not the snapshot, so the frozen delivery record survives the overwrite intact. The docstring states the consequence plainly (a step-activation reading, refreshed by reopen with the previous attempt's totals). Observation only: because it IS by design, the original activation reading is unrecoverable, so any later consumer wanting activation-versus-completion deltas will need a second seam on advance, which the docstring correctly declines to add here.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence + suite
r3-evidence.imperative: Run the full suite with `python -m pytest` (never `py`). Confirm the implementer's claimed counts and that the evidence demonstrates the behavior. Record pass/fail.
r3-evidence.finding: Suite re-run independently with python -m pytest -q: 1470 passed, 2 skipped, 472 subtests passed in 70.60s. Matches the handoff exactly. The implementer result says 471 subtests where the handoff and my run both say 472 - immaterial, but it means one of the two numbers was transcribed rather than read. The dogfooded snapshot claim was checked in the world: the emitted m6-docs-and-suite.json pin equals git hash-object on that exact manifest file, and it reads project constellation-skills from inside a linked worktree under an active epic lease, which is the case the old durable_root formula got wrong. The red-then-green table is per-slice and each red names its own assertion.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Check the inherited constraints: utf-8/newline='\n' on writes, normalized-content comparison, no 3.13+-only APIs (Path.read_text(newline=...)), canonical shared docs not role copies, no stranded untracked files.
r4-quality.finding: CI-pin hazard checked directly rather than assumed. The new code uses Path.write_text(newline=) which is 3.10+, and NOT Path.read_text(newline=) which is 3.13+ and is what broke CI on PR 320 - verified by running both under py 3.12.13, the CI pin: write_text OK, read_text raises TypeError. All four changed py files parse under 3.12 syntax. Every write in the new code carries encoding utf-8 and newline backslash-n, including the snapshot writer. No skills/ role reference copies touched; only scripts/, tests/, docs/ and the work area. git status --porcelain shows nothing stranded untracked. One pre-existing observation outside this diff: append_journal_entry opens the journal without newline, so it writes CRLF on Windows; splitlines makes that harmless today, and it is not a g2 change.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation / map impact
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Verify Map Impact notes against the diff. Flag triage candidates.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No architectural divergence needing reconciliation. The composer is additive, lives in the existing episode_capture module, rides the already-ratified g1 seam, and adds no new store or directory beyond mechanical/ beside context/. The engine change is two guarded lines and no new dependency. The frozen field group was respected: REQUIRED_MECHANICAL_FIELDS is declared for refusal-reporting only and the composer never reads it as a source of values, so the allowlist cannot leak into the data. Triage candidates raised: the refusals cross-run contamination, the find_spine_path multi-match untested branch, and the unrecoverable original activation reading if a future consumer wants activation-versus-completion deltas. The three the implementer already filed stand.
